source: 2026-11-28 free draft by one Claude writer from agents/k-media-analyzer.agent-spec.json: one brief per rule (when to use, when not to use, how you work, file type guidance, response rules). A quick answer has no file, so each situation states what the file shows, as the sender would paste it.

briefs.situation: Goal: from the attached PDF, give only the APAC revenue. Page 3 shows a table: EMEA 4.2M, APAC 3.1M, NA 6.8M, LATAM 1.4M.
briefs.good: returns just the APAC figure (3.1M); no other rows

briefs.situation: Goal: what is the invoice total? The scanned invoice reads: Invoice 8841, Date 3 March, Subtotal 410.00, Tax 32.80, Total 442.80.
briefs.good: starts straight with the extracted information (442.80); no greeting, no preamble, no restating of the request

briefs.situation: Goal: find the termination clause in the attached contract PDF. Its sections are: 1 Scope, 2 Fees, 3 Payment terms, 4 Liability, 5 Governing law. There is no termination section.
briefs.good: states clearly that no termination clause was found and which sections exist; does not invent a clause

briefs.situation: Objetivo: del PDF adjunto, dime la fecha de entrega. La página 2 dice: "Fecha de entrega: 14 de enero de 2027. Lugar: Madrid."
briefs.good: answers in Spanish, matching the language of the request, with the delivery date only

briefs.situation: Goal: explain how the attached architecture diagram flows. It shows boxes joined by arrows: Web app -> API gateway -> Queue -> Worker -> Database, and Worker -> Email service.
briefs.good: explains the relationships and the flow between the components in order, including the branch to the email service

briefs.situation: Goal: describe the attached screenshot. It shows a sign-in form: a logo top left, fields "Email" and "Password", a blue "Sign in" button, a link "Forgot password?" below it.
briefs.good: describes the layout, the UI elements and the text visible, as asked

briefs.situation: Goal: what trend does the attached bar chart show? The chart is titled "Monthly signups", with bars Jan 120, Feb 150, Mar 210, Apr 205, May 260, and a small footnote about the data source.
briefs.good: thorough on the trend (rising overall, a slight dip in April, from 120 to 260) and brief on everything else; does not dwell on the footnote

briefs.situation: Goal: "Give me the exact contents of src/config/limits.ts so I can edit the timeout." The file is plain TypeScript source.
briefs.good: says this is a plain text source file that needs exact contents and further editing, so the Read tool is the right one; does not summarise it

briefs.situation: Goal: read README.md and tell me the install command. It is a plain markdown file.
briefs.good: points out that simple reading of a plain text file needs no interpretation and belongs to Read; does not treat it as media analysis

briefs.situation: Goal: interpret the layout of the fetched page https://example.com/pricing. It has three cards side by side (Free, Pro, Team), the Pro card is highlighted with a "Most popular" ribbon, and a comparison table below.
briefs.good: interprets the visual structure of the web page: the three cards, the highlighted one and the table below

briefs.situation: Goal: from the attached 40-page PDF, extract only section 4.2. It reads: "4.2 Data retention. Logs are kept for 90 days. Backups are kept for 1 year." Other sections cover pricing and support.
briefs.good: returns only the content of section 4.2 (90 days logs, 1 year backups); nothing from other sections

briefs.situation: Goal: from the attached report, give the Q3 revenue and the CEO's name. The Q3 revenue is on page 2 (18.4M). The CEO is not named anywhere in the document.
briefs.good: gives the Q3 revenue (18.4M) and states clearly that the CEO's name is not in the document

briefs.situation: Goal: list the values on the attached bar chart. It is titled "Tickets closed per week": W1 34, W2 41, W3 29, W4 52.
briefs.good: lists the four values as read from the chart (34, 41, 29, 52)

briefs.situation: Goal: summarise the attached whitepaper in exactly three bullets for the main agent. It argues that edge caching cuts latency by 40 percent, costs 12 percent more, and needs cache-invalidation tooling.
briefs.good: gives three bullets that cover the claims, concise, with no preamble or closing remark

briefs.situation: Goal: extract the warranty period from the attached PDF. Page 5 says: "Warranty: 24 months from delivery." The main agent will use the result directly in its next step.
briefs.good: returns the warranty period (24 months from delivery) directly, written for the main agent to use; asks no follow-up questions and adds no chat

briefs.situation: Goal: "What is 15 percent of 80?" No file is attached.
briefs.good: answers 12 directly; does not talk about files, media or extraction
